newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver ends up, gold steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver ends up, gold steady.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) prices close 15 rupees higher at 7,440 rupees per kg, after opening lower by 20 rupees at 7,405 rupees.
** Gold 24 carat closed steady in limited trade at 4,800 rupees per 10 grammes after opening steady at 4,800 rupees.
** Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) closed steady at 56,100 rupees per piece.
Silver (.999) closed 15 rupees higher at 7,440 rupees per kg on the back of lower than expected imports and shortage of ready stock, dealers said.
In early trade silver opened 20 rupees lower at 7,405 rupees per kg on profit-taking following a slight setback in global markets, dealers said.
"But prices bounced back towards close on fresh industrial buying and shortage of ready stock," said a dealer. "Poor arrivals also trimmed early losses."
Silver was up by 40 rupees per kg on Tuesday.
Gold 24 carat closed steady at 4,800 rupees per 10 grammes after opening at the same level, dealers said.
"Trade was quiet during the day amid scattered arrivals and seasonal buying was at a low ebb," said a dealer.
Gold was up by 20 rupees per 10 gramme on Tuesday.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) closed steady at 56,100 rupees per piece. They were up by 200 rupees per piece on Tuesday.
"Actually gold is consolidating recent gains and may move up again on seasonal buying in the coming days," one broker said.
